key_insight: HVAF-sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr achieved the lowest reported wear rate and best corrosion resistance, while HVOF produced the highest hardness.
engineering_relevance: HVAF is a promising coating route for 304 stainless steel components requiring combined wear and corrosion protection.
method: Deposited WC-10Co-4Cr on 304 stainless steel using APS, detonation, HVOF and HVAF spraying.
Compared coating microstructure, Vickers hardness, friction and volumetric wear.
Evaluated corrosion potential, current density and corrosion resistance.
evidence_signal: HVAF showed a wear rate of (1.10±0.01)×10⁻⁵ mm³/(N·m), versus (36.82±0.80)×10⁻⁵ for uncoated steel, and the lowest coating corrosion current density at 1.75±0.02 μA/cm².
watch_item: The abstract does not specify wear or corrosion test conditions, limiting direct transfer of these rankings to service environments.
paper_title: Microstructure, Wear and Corrosion Resistances of Atmospheric Plasma, Detonation, High Velocity Oxy-fuel and High Velocity Air-fuel Sprayed WC-10Co-4Cr Cemented Carbide Coatings
